focus: Claude Code ask surface (AskUserQuestion) and Stop-hook enforcement
noveltyJustification: Seven new findings: the exact Claude Code tool name, its subagent exclusion, the timeout setting, the Stop block contract, the all-async local Stop wiring, the advisory sentinel shape, and the registry field that controls blocking.
ruledOut: transcript_path for last-message recovery (racy at Stop)
PostToolUse on AskUserQuestion as the enforcement point (cannot see a turn with no tool call)

label: Claude Code's native ask tool is AskUserQuestion: multiple-choice, permission not required, exact tool-name string used by matchers and permission rules.
AskUserQuestion is removed from every subagent's tool pool even when listed in tools, so only the main conversation can ask the operator.
askUserQuestionTimeout (60s, 5m, 10m) can auto-close a question and let Claude continue; it never starts in background sessions, screen-reader mode or Remote Control.
Claude Stop hooks can block with decision:block plus reason; last_assistant_message carries the final text and stop_hook_active guards re-entry, with an 8-continuation cap.
All three Claude Stop hooks in .claude/settings.json are async:true, so no existing Stop hook can block; the known failure evidence is confirmed.
The completion-evidence Stop sentinel is the reusable adapter shape: stdin payload, stop_hook_active no-op, last_assistant_message claim detection, and an explicit never-block policy.
Blocking is one registry field: hook-registry.json binding.async drives hook.async in the generated .claude/settings.json via sync-hook-registrations.cjs.

direction: Recovering the last assistant message from transcript_path at Stop time
reason: The hooks reference says the transcript is written asynchronously and may lag the current turn; last_assistant_message is the documented source.

direction: Enforcing the ask surface from PostToolUse on AskUserQuestion
reason: PostToolUse only fires when a tool ran; the failure case is a turn that ends with no ask-tool call at all.
